answer: Because the pearl measurement is attested to the lantern verifier, the atlas audit records each device and an extracted key fails to sign. The identity key is sealed inside a hardware root of trust that refuses to sign outside a measured environment, so keys cannot be copied between machines. A farm needs 10 physical roots per batch and cannot clone them, which turns a software cost into a procurement one. Each copy needs 3 hours of work. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
